cities.name: Oakland & the Bay Area
cities.heading: Where the Party began
cities.body: Huey P. Newton and Bobby Seale founded the Party here in October 1966. Oakland became its national center.

cities.name: Los Angeles
cities.heading: Organizing under pressure
cities.body: Breakfast and medical programs developed alongside organizing repeatedly disrupted by police raids and conflict.

cities.name: Chicago
cities.heading: Coalitions across communities
cities.body: The Illinois Panthers built multiracial alliances through the Rainbow Coalition and organized food and health programs.

cities.name: New York
cities.heading: Neighborhoods and defense campaigns
cities.body: Harlem anchored a network of neighborhood offices. Defense of the Panther 21 became a major organizing focus.

cities.name: Seattle
cities.heading: A lasting community presence
cities.body: The Seattle chapter combined police accountability work with health care, meals and youth education.

cities.name: Philadelphia
cities.heading: Political education in practice
cities.body: The local organization provided food, clothing, a clinic, political classes and a library of Black authors.

events.title: The Party is founded
events.body: Huey P. Newton and Bobby Seale establish the Black Panther Party for Self Defense in Oakland.

events.title: A protest reaches Sacramento
events.body: Bobby Seale leads Panthers to the California State Capitol to oppose proposed restrictions on carrying loaded firearms.

events.title: A growing Los Angeles organization
events.body: The Los Angeles organization gains hundreds of recruits under new leadership.

events.title: A chapter takes shape in Philadelphia
events.body: The Philadelphia chapter forms and soon adds a second office.

events.title: Fred Hampton joins the Illinois Panthers
events.body: Hampton brings experience in youth organizing and soon becomes deputy chairman of the Illinois chapter.

events.title: Seattle Panthers demonstrate in Olympia
events.body: Members appear at the Washington State Capitol during a dispute over firearms restrictions—the moment pictured above.

events.title: The Panther 21 prosecution
events.body: An alleged bombing conspiracy prosecution makes prisoner defense a focus of New York organizing.

events.title: Fred Hampton and Mark Clark are killed
events.body: Police kill Hampton and Clark in a raid. National Archives records document FBI infiltration and the subsequent civil-rights case.

events.title: Seattle expands community services
events.body: Seattle Panthers operate a community medical clinic alongside food and youth programs.

events.title: The Intercommunal Youth Institute opens
events.body: The educational project that later becomes the Oakland Community School opens, connecting learning, child care and community life.

events.title: An East Coast split
events.body: New York breaks with Oakland and begins publishing Right On.

events.title: Ericka Huggins directs the Oakland Community School
events.body: Huggins leads the school through years of teaching, care and community-centered education.

events.title: Programs outlast the chapter
events.body: Seattle’s community programs continue beyond the chapter.

platform.title: Community self-determination
platform.body: Black communities should control their own political future.

platform.title: Work and income
platform.body: Employment or guaranteed income should make a decent livelihood possible.

platform.title: An end to exploitation
platform.body: The platform challenges capitalist extraction and demands restitution for historical theft.

platform.title: Housing with dignity
platform.body: Safe housing should meet human needs, with cooperative ownership proposed as a remedy.

platform.title: Education and history
platform.body: Education should teach Black history and equip people to understand their position in society.

platform.title: Opposition to conscription
platform.body: Black men should not be compelled to fight for a government that denies their rights.

platform.title: Safety from police violence
platform.body: Communities should be protected from police brutality and killings.

platform.title: Freedom for imprisoned Black people
platform.body: The Party demands release, arguing that Black prisoners have been denied fair trials.

platform.title: Juries from the community
platform.body: Defendants should be judged by peers who understand their communities and circumstances.

platform.title: The material conditions of freedom
platform.body: Basic necessities, justice and peace belong together in the Party’s vision of liberation.
